:::{#exm-weibull-ph-aft}
#### A hazard ratio of 4 with Weibull shape 2

Take $\lambda = 0.05$, $p = 2$, and $\theta_i = 4$,
with time in weeks.
By @thm-weibull-ph-aft, the acceleration factor is

$$
\ba
\theta_i^{1/p}
&= 4^{1/2}
&& \text{(substitute } \theta_i = 4,\ p = 2 \text{)} \\
&= 2
&& \text{(square root)}
\ea
$$

To check, compute subject $i$'s survival at 10 weeks both ways:

$$
\ba
\sb{\surv_0(10)}^{\theta_i}
&= \sb{\expf{-(0.05 \cdot 10)^2}}^{4}
&& \text{(proportional hazards form)} \\
&= \expf{-4 \cdot 0.25}
&& \text{(} (0.5)^2 = 0.25 \text{; exponent laws)} \\
&= \expf{-1}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
\surv_0(10 \cdot 2)
&= \expf{-(0.05 \cdot 20)^2}
&& \text{(AFT form with acceleration factor 2)} \\
&= \expf{-1}
&& \text{(} (1)^2 = 1 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Both forms give $\expf{-1} \approx 0.368$:
a four-fold hazard means that subject $i$ ages twice as fast as baseline.

:::
